# Basic Graphs {#sec-graphs-basic}

The graphs in this chapter are available from the `r keys("Basic")` button in the **Graphs** section of the **Analyses** tab.
Along with the options described here, each graph's editor includes the [shared pages](#sec-editor-common) (e.g., **Axes**, **Legend**, and **Placement**).

## Bar Chart {#sec-bar-chart-dlg}

A bar chart compares categories with one bar each.
Each bar is sized by either how many rows fall into the category or by the total of a measurement.
Bars can optionally be split into blocks.
The dataset should have one row per observation, holding its category and (optionally) a measurement to add up and the group that it belongs to.

### Variables {-}

**Category**: The categories to compare.
Each unique value becomes one bar.

**Weight** (optional): A measurement to add up for each category.
Without it, the bars show how many rows fall into each category.

**Group** (optional): Splits each bar into blocks, one per unique value (e.g., the portion of each bar contributed by each gender).

### Options {-}

**Orientation**: Select whether the bars are drawn **Horizontal** or **Vertical**.

**Bar labels**: Select the label shown on each bar (**Value**, **Percentage**, **Value and Percentage**, **No Display**, **Name**, **Name and Value**, or **Name and Percentage**).

**Apply color scheme to ungrouped bars**: Check this option to color each bar from the color scheme when no group is used.
Otherwise, all bars use the same color.

**Constrain axis to bar lengths**: Check this option to force the scaling axis to the length of the longest bar.
This is only recommended when the scaling axis is not shown and the bars are being used for artistic purposes.

**Include spaces between bars**: Check this option to draw a space between each bar.

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Fold over-long bars
:::

Select how bars that are vastly longer than the others are drawn:

**None**: No bars are folded.

**Serpentine**: A long bar is folded back and forth through blank rows that are inserted beneath it.

**Aggressive serpentine**: A long bar is folded, with its last fold packed into the free space of a row that already holds a shorter bar.
Blank rows are only added when no row has room.
::::

**Fold threshold**: Enter how many times longer than the other bars a bar must be to be folded.
A bar is folded when its length is at least this many times the length of the longest bar that is not folded.
The default is 3.

**Show fold direction arrows**: Check this option to draw arrows showing the direction that a folded bar continues in.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
Folding requires at least two bars and a scaling axis that is not reversed.
A bar can only be folded if it is a single block and is not part of a bar group.
Effects such as images, stipples, and gradients are not applied to folded bars.
:::

**Bar label suffix**: Enter text to add to the end of each bar's label (e.g., *%* or *units*).

**Bar effect**: Select how the bars are drawn.
These are the same effects as the [**Box Plot**](#sec-box-plot-dlg)'s **Box effect** option.

### Bar Shapes {-}

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Shape
:::

**Same shape for all bars**: Select the shape used for every bar:

- **Rectangle**: A rectangle (the default).
- **Arrow**: An arrow pointing to the right (horizontal bars) or up (vertical bars).
- **Reverse Arrow**: An arrow pointing to the left (horizontal bars) or down (vertical bars).

**Custom per-bar shapes**: Add bars that should use a different shape than the others.
::::

**Bar block decals**: Add text to write on a bar's block.
Select the **Bar** and **Block**, then enter the **Text**.

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Bar Sorting
:::

**No custom sort**: Select this option to keep the bars in their default order.

**Sort by**: Select this option to sort the bars by their **Bar length** or their **Bar label**, in either **Ascending** or **Descending** order.

**Custom order**: Select this option to arrange the bars in your own order.
::::

### Bar Groups {-}

A bar group wraps a curly brace around a contiguous series of bars.
On the other side of the brace, a bar is drawn showing the combined length of the bars within the group.
This is useful for drawing attention to a block of smaller bars that may be eclipsed by a larger bar.

When adding a bar group, the following options are available:

- **Start bar**: The first bar in the group.
- **End bar**: The last bar in the group.
- **Label**: The label drawn on the group's bar.
- **Color**: The color of the group's bar.
  Check **Custom** to select your own color, otherwise the color scheme is used.

### Showcasing {-}

**Ghost opacity**: Enter the opacity of the bars that are not showcased.
A value of 0 is fully transparent, whereas 255 is fully opaque.

**Hide labels on non-showcased bars**: Check this option to remove the labels from the ghosted bars.

**Showcase bars**: Add the bars to showcase.
These bars are drawn fully opaque, and all others are drawn with the ghost opacity.

\newpage

## Pie Chart {#sec-pie-chart-dlg}

A pie chart shows how a total is divided among groups, as slices of a pie.
Subgroups can be added as an inner ring.
The dataset should have a column of groups, either with one row per observation (which are counted) or one row per group with a column of values to add up.

### Variables {-}

**Group (outer)**: The groups that become the slices of the pie.

**Weight** (optional): The value to add up for each group.
If omitted, then the rows of each group are counted.

**Subgroup (inner)** (optional): Splits each slice into subgroups, which are drawn as an inner ring lined up against their parent slices.

### Options {-}

**Style**: Select a decorative style for the pie (e.g., *Clockface*, *Cheese pizza*, *Chocolate chip cookie*, or *Pumpkin pie*).
Select **None** for a standard pie chart.

### Labels {-}

**Outer midpoint**: Select the label shown in the middle of the outer slices (**Value**, **Percentage**, **Value & percentage**, **No labels**, **Name**, **Name & value**, or **Name & percentage**).

**Outer**: Select the label shown outside of the outer slices.

**Inner midpoint**: Select the label shown in the middle of the inner slices.

**Placement**: Select where the outer labels are placed:

- **Next to slice**: The labels are next to their slices.
- **Flush**: The labels are flush with the left and right sides of the plot area.

**Show outer pie labels**: Check this option to show the outer slices' labels.

**Show inner pie labels**: Check this option to show the inner slices' labels.

**Color-matched labels**: Check this option to have the outer labels' font colors match their slices.

### Donut Hole {-}

**Include donut hole**: Check this option to draw a hole in the middle of the pie.

**Background color**: Select the color of the donut hole.

**Hole proportion**: Enter the size of the hole, as a proportion of the pie.

**Edit Label...**: Click this button to edit the label shown inside the donut hole.

### Showcasing {-}

**Ghost opacity**: Enter the opacity of the slices that are not showcased.

**Mode**: Select which slices to showcase:

- **None**: No slices are showcased.
- **Explicit list of outer slices**: Showcases the slices listed in **Slices to showcase**.
- **Largest outer slice(s)** / **Smallest outer slice(s)**: Showcases the largest (or smallest) outer slices.
- **Largest inner slice(s)** / **Smallest inner slice(s)**: Showcases the largest (or smallest) inner slices.

**Ring labels shown**: Select which ring's labels are shown while showcasing (**Inner** or **Outer**).

**Group by outer slice**: Check this option to find the largest (or smallest) inner slices within each outer slice, rather than across the whole pie.

**Show outer pie midpoint labels while showcasing**: Check this option to keep the outer slices' midpoint labels.

**Slices to showcase**: Add the outer slices to showcase.

### Slice Images {-}

**Effect**: Select whether the slices are drawn with a **Solid** color or an **Image**.

**Images (blank rows use the brush)**: Select an image for each slice.
Slices with a blank row will use the regular color.

\newpage

## Line Plot {#sec-line-plot-dlg}

A line plot shows how a measurement changes across a series (e.g., weeks or years), with an optional separate line for each group.
The dataset should have one row per point, holding the measurement, its position along the x axis, and optionally the group that the point belongs to.

### Variables {-}

**Values**: The measurement being plotted on the y axis (e.g., an average grade).

**Series**: The position of each point along the x axis (e.g., a week or a year).

**Grouping** (optional): Draws a separate line for each unique value (e.g., one line per gender).
Without it, a single line is drawn.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
Row order matters.
Each line is drawn through its points in the order that they appear in the dataset, not sorted by the x axis.
A missing value breaks the line at that row, and the next valid row starts the line again.
:::

### Options {-}

**Auto spline**: Check this option to draw a line as a spline when it zigzags (i.e., goes back and forth along the x axis).
This is useful for lines that show a downward spiral.

### Showcasing {-}

**Ghost opacity**: Enter the opacity of the lines that are not showcased.

**Showcase lines**: Add the lines (by group) to showcase.

\newpage

## Multi-Series Line Plot {#sec-multi-series-line-plot-dlg}

A multi-series line plot compares several measurements across the same x axis, with a separate line for each measurement column.
The dataset should have one row per position along the x axis, with a column for the x value and a column for each measurement to plot.

### Variables {-}

**Y (series)**: The measurements to plot.
Each column you select is drawn as its own line.

**X (axis)**: The position of each point along the x axis (e.g., a quarter or a year).
All the lines share it.

### Options {-}

**Auto spline**: The same as the [**Line Plot**](#sec-line-plot-dlg) option.

\newpage

## Table {#sec-table-dlg}

A table shows the values of a dataset as a formatted grid.

**Dataset**: Select the dataset to show.

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Columns Selection
:::

**All columns**: Select this option to include every column.

**Custom selection**: Select this option to choose the columns.
Click `r keys("Variables...")` to select them.
::::

### Header & Layout {-}

**Transpose**: Check this option to swap the table's rows and columns.

**Bold header row**: Check this option to make the first row bold.

**Center header row**: Check this option to center the first row.

**Bold first column**: Check this option to make the first column bold.

### Appearance {-}

**Alternate row colors**: Check this option to shade every other row.

**Clear trailing row formatting**: Check this option to hide the formatting (e.g., borders and alternating row colors) for any rows beyond the data.
This is only relevant if the table is larger than its data.

### Sizing {-}

**Minimum width (%)**: Enter the minimum percentage of its area's width that the table should consume.
By default, the table fits its content.

**Minimum height (%)**: Enter the minimum percentage of its area's height that the table should consume.

### Footnotes {-}

A footnote adds a citation number after a value in the table, with the footnote shown in the caption.

- **Value**: The value (as displayed) to look for in the table.
- **Footnote**: The footnote's text.

Up to twenty footnotes are supported.
If the value is not found in the table, then the footnote is not added.

### Aggregates {-}

An aggregate is a row or column of calculated values (e.g., a total).

- **Name**: The label for the aggregate.
- **Type**: Whether to add a **Column** or **Row**.
- **Aggregate Type**:
  - **Total**: Sums a series of values.
  - **Change %**: The change from one value to another, as a percentage.
  - **Ratio**: The ratio between two values.
  - **Change**: The change (i.e., difference) from one value to another.
- **Start** and **End**: The first and last rows or columns to calculate from.
  These can be positions or names.
- **Start Offset** and **End Offset**: The number of rows or columns to shift the start and end positions by.
- **Use adjacent cell color**: Check this option to use the color of the neighboring cells.
- **Background Color**: The background color of the aggregate's cells.
  This is ignored if **Use adjacent cell color** is checked.

### Cell Annotations {-}

A cell annotation highlights one or more cells and adds a note pointing to them.

- **Annotation text**: The note's text.
- **Side**: Whether the note is placed to the **Left** or **Right** of the table.
- **Background color**: The color used to highlight the cells.
- **Cell selection**: Which cells to highlight:
  - **Column outliers**: The outliers in a column (select the **Column name**).
  - **Column top-N**: The largest values in a column (select the **Column name** and enter the **N (top count)**).
  - **Cell range**: A range of cells (enter the **Start cell** and **End cell**).

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
If the table's minimum width is set to fill the entire width, then it will be turned off when annotations are added, so that there is room for the notes.
:::

\newpage

## Sankey Diagram {#sec-sankey-dlg}

A Sankey diagram shows how a set of starting groups flows into a set of ending groups, with the width of each flow showing its size.
The dataset should have a column of starting groups and a column of ending groups.
Each row is either one observation, or a group with its totals if weight columns are supplied.

### Variables {-}

**From**: The starting groups, shown on the left side of the diagram.

**To**: The ending groups, shown on the right side of the diagram.

**From weight** (optional): The size of each starting group.
If omitted, then the rows of each group are counted.

**To weight** (optional): The size of each ending group.
If omitted, then the rows of each group are counted.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
**From weight** and **To weight** must be used together.
:::

**From group** (optional): Sorts the starting groups into larger groups (e.g., schools by county), which are labeled with brackets on the left.

### Options {-}

**Flow shape**: Select whether the flows are drawn **Curvy** or **Jagged**.

**Group labels**: Select the label shown on each group (**Name**, **Value**, **Percentage**, **Name & Value**, **Name & Percentage**, **Value & Percentage**, or **No Display**).

**Column headers**: Select whether the column labels are shown **As Header** or **As Footer**, or select **No Display** to hide them.
Enter the labels for each column in the **Column Labels** list.

### Showcasing {-}

**Ghost opacity**: Enter the opacity of the streams that are not showcased.

**Also ghost "To" labels**: Check this option to also ghost the labels of the ending groups that are not showcased.

**"To" labels to showcase**: Add the ending groups whose streams should be showcased.

\newpage

## Waffle Chart {#sec-waffle-dlg}

A waffle chart arranges repeated shapes into a square-like grid.
Rather than using a dataset, it is built from a list of shapes, each with the number of times it should repeat.

**Shapes**: The list of shapes to draw across the grid.
Click the new button to add a shape, and double-click a shape to edit it.

### Grid Rounding {-}

**Round grid to a fixed cell count**: Check this option to make sure that a specific number of cells are drawn.
If the shapes' total repeat count is less than this, then extra cells are added to a shape.
If the total is more, then cells are removed from that shape.
This is useful when each cell represents a percentage and the cells do not add up to 100 because of rounding.

**Cell count**: Enter the number of cells for the grid.

**Shape index**: Enter which shape (by its position in the list) to add or remove cells from.

### Row Count {-}

**Specify row count**: Check this option to set the number of rows that the shapes are split into.
By default, the grid has an equal number of rows and columns.

**Rows**: Enter the number of rows.

\newpage

## Race Track Chart {#sec-race-track-dlg}

A race track chart compares amounts as concentric circular track lanes, each one extending around the circle in proportion to its value.
The dataset should have one row per lane, holding its name and its value.
The first row is the outermost lane.

### Variables {-}

**Value**: The amount for each lane.
The longest lane goes almost all the way around, and the others are drawn in proportion.

**Label**: The name of each lane.

### Options {-}

**Tracks**: Select how many concentric tracks to spread the lanes across (**Automatic**, **One**, or **Two**).
**Automatic** decides based on how narrow the smallest lane would be.

**Start angle (degrees)**: Enter the angle that the lanes start at.

**Track proportion**: Enter the proportion of the plot area used for the track (versus the hole in the middle).

**Show track lane labels**: Check this option to label each lane.

\newpage

## Nightingale Rose Chart {#sec-nightingale-rose-dlg}

A Nightingale rose chart shows values by category as wedges around a circle, where the radius of each wedge represents its amount.
It can include a series within each slice.
The dataset should have one row per observation, holding its category and (optionally) an amount to add up and the series that it belongs to.

### Variables {-}

**Category**: The categories that become the slices around the circle (e.g., the months of a year).

**Aggregate** (optional): A measurement to add up for each slice.
Without it, the wedges show how many rows fall into each category.

**Series** (optional): Splits each slice into a wedge for each unique value (e.g., the cause of each death).

### Options {-}

**Radial scaling**: Select how a wedge's value maps to its radius:

- **Area proportional**: The wedge's area is proportional to its value.
- **Radius proportional**: The wedge's radius is proportional to its value.

**Series display**: Select how the series are drawn:

- **Overlaid**: All wedges start at the center, with larger ones behind smaller ones.
- **Stacked**: Each series is a band on top of the previous one.

**Start angle (degrees)**: Enter the angle that the first slice starts at.

**Show category labels**: Check this option to label each slice.

### Ghosting {-}

**Ghost opacity**: Enter the opacity of the ghosted wedges.

**Wedges to ghost (series / category)**: Add the wedges to ghost.
Leave the category blank to ghost the series in every slice.

\newpage

## Du Bois Spiral Chart {#sec-du-bois-spiral-dlg}

A Du Bois spiral chart draws values as segments of one long path that zigzags down and then winds into a spiral.
The first segment is drawn horizontally across the top, the middle segments zigzag diagonally downward, and the last segment winds inward as a spiral.
This suits data where the last value is far larger than the others, as the spiral can absorb a very long length in a compact area.
The dataset should have one row per segment, in the order that the segments should be drawn, holding its name and its value.

The layout follows W. E. B. Du Bois's *City and Rural Population. 1890* [@battle-baptiste-rusert], one of the hand-drawn plates that he and his students at Atlanta University prepared for the 1900 Paris Exposition.

### Variables {-}

**Label**: The name of each segment.

**Value**: The amount for each segment.
The length of the segment is proportional to it.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
Row order matters.
The first row is drawn across the top, and the last row is drawn as the innermost part of the spiral.
Rows with a missing, zero, or negative value are skipped.
Each segment is colored from the color scheme, based on its position along the path.
:::

### Options {-}

**Value display**: Select how the segments' values are formatted in their labels:

- **Value**: The value as-is (e.g., *1,204*).
  Whole numbers are shown without decimals.
- **Percentage**: The value as a percentage.
  The values should be proportions, as they are multiplied by 100 (e.g., *0.25* is shown as *25%*).
- **Currency**: The value as currency, using your system's currency symbol.
  Cents are only shown if the value has them.

**Zigzag angle (degrees)**: Enter the angle (below horizontal) that the middle segments zigzag downward at.
Smaller angles make flatter, wider zigzags, whereas larger angles make steeper, narrower ones.
This can range from 10 to 80, and the default is 40.

**Spiral radius (%)**: Enter the outer radius of the spiral, as a percentage of the plot's smaller dimension (i.e., its width or height).
This can range from 15 to 48, and the default is 36.

**Line thickness (%)**: Enter the thickness of the path, as a percentage of the plot's smaller dimension.
This can range from 0.5 to 8, and the default is 2.5.

**Show labels**: Check this option to label each segment with its value and name (e.g., *1,204: Under 2,500*).

\newpage

## Dueling Pie Chart {#sec-dueling-pie-dlg}

A dueling pie chart compares how two groups divide a whole, with a pie for each group using the same categories for the slices.
The dataset should have one row per category per group, holding the category, the group, and the value.

### Variables {-}

**Category**: The categories that become the slices in each pie (e.g., activities).

**Group**: The group that each value belongs to.
Each group gets its own pie, and there must be exactly two groups.

**Value**: The amount for each category within each group (e.g., hours).

### Options {-}

**Slice labels**: Select the label shown on each slice (**Percentage**, **Value**, or **Value and percentage**).

\newpage

## Pictograph {#sec-pictograph-dlg}

A pictograph compares amounts using a row of icons, where the size of each icon reflects its value.
The dataset should have one row per icon, holding its label and its value.
No more than 10 rows can be shown.

### Variables {-}

**Label**: The name of each observation.
Each row is drawn as its own icon.

**Value**: The amount for each observation.
The area of its icon is proportional to it.

### Options {-}

**Icon Shape**: Select the shape used for the icons.

**Orientation**: Select whether the icons are arranged **Vertical** or **Horizontal**.

**Value display**: Select how values are shown (**Value**, **Percentage**, or **Currency**).

**Fill color**: Select the color of the icons.

**Outline color**: Select the color of the icons' outlines.

\newpage

## Choropleth Map {#sec-choropleth-dlg}

A choropleth map shades the regions of a map (e.g., states or counties) by a measurement or by the group that each region belongs to.
The region shapes come from a KML or GeoJSON file.
A dataset is optional, and holds one or more rows per region with the region's name and its values.

### Regions {-}

**Regions (KML or GeoJSON file)**: Select the file that holds the region shapes.

**Region key field**: Select the field in the file that holds the regions' names.
This is used to match the regions against the dataset's key column.

**Background layer (optional)**: Select a second KML or GeoJSON file to draw beneath the regions as a backdrop (e.g., a state outline or the neighboring regions).
This keeps a map with gaps from floating on the page.

### Data to Map {-}

**Dataset**: Select the dataset holding the regions' values, or **(none)** to only draw the regions.

Click `r keys("Select columns...")` to select the following columns:

- **Key column**: The name of the region that each row belongs to (e.g., a state).
  It is matched against the region key field of the map file.
- **Value column**: The measurement that each region is shaded by (e.g., a population).
  When a group column is also used, it sets the opacity of each group's color instead.
- **Group column**: Colors each region by the group that it belongs to (e.g., a sales territory).
- **Symbol size column**: A second measurement, shown as a circle at the center of each region with its area proportional to the value.

**Combine rows per region**: If the dataset has several rows for a region, then select how they are combined into one number (sum, mean, minimum, maximum, or count).

**Value format**: Select how values are shown (**Value**, **Currency**, or **Simple value**).

### Other Options {-}

**Proportional symbols**: **Symbol color** selects the color of the proportional symbol circles.

**Regions with no data**: Select how regions without a value are filled (**Solid color** or one of the hatch patterns).

**Show latitude and longitude grid**: Check this option to draw a faint latitude and longitude grid over the map.
Each grid line is labeled with its coordinate.

**Show only regions that have a value**: Check this option to only draw the regions that have a mapped value.
